meta.title: NYSC Strategic Deployment
meta.blurb: 500 graduates to 750 primary health facilities by specialization and disease burden
meta.banner: Recorded run of the NYSC deployment research. Every figure is from the invention disclosure.
meta.replayLabel: Recorded run replay, not a live solve
meta.sampleLabel: Illustrative sample: produced by a script over real facility and graduate rows, not output of the recorded run
meta.confidentialBanner: Confidential. Supporting document for an application. Do not redistribute.

evolution.name: Genetic algorithm heuristic
evolution.did: Random starting plans scored on skill-match reward minus overload and mismatch penalties; improved by selection, recombination and mutation.
evolution.exposed: Random starts wasted generations on overloaded, mismatched plans.

evolution.name: Version 2
evolution.did: Greedy starting plans, plus a classifier that labelled assignments Good or Poor for repair.
evolution.exposed: The classifier memorized hand-written rules (100% accuracy) and its repairs fought the search. Greedy starts left 146 overloads and 91 mismatches.

evolution.name: Version 3
evolution.did: A model trained on the search's own score predicts how good a single move is; mixed starting population; changes kept only if the real score improves.
evolution.exposed: No way to carry decisions already made.

evolution.name: Version 4
evolution.did: Decisions already made stay fixed; the 500 graduates are placed in five ordered batches; final passes fill empty facilities and clear over-capacity ones.
evolution.exposed: The need to measure and verify outcomes, which became the Intellign platform layer.

evolution.name: Intellign platform (2026)
evolution.did: Plain-language front end, gated pipeline, checks before and after solving, several solvers.
evolution.exposed: Current embodiment. 2,531 backend tests passed; contract pipeline replayed over 91 cached live sessions.

mechanism: The engine searches many possible deployments and keeps improving the best ones.
A learned model predicts whether moving one graduate to a different facility would make the plan better, so the search spends less time on bad moves.
Placements already decided stay fixed while the rest are solved in batches, so a reviewer can pin a person to a site and everything else adapts.
A final check recomputes the real score and keeps a change only if it helps, then removes anyone assigned to an over-capacity facility.
limits: The graduate records are generated, and facility capacity, staffing, specialization and disease fields are augmented.
The learned model's contribution has not been isolated by an ablation, and no timing comparison against exact move scoring has been recorded.
During the version 4 run, model-guided repairs inside the search were rare (zero or one per batch).
The version 4 model evaluation output was not retained; the model figures shown are from the version 3 run.
Version 4 matches version 3 on skill match (409 of 500). Its recorded gain is structural: fixed decisions, staged batches, and no assigned graduate placed in an over-capacity facility.

goals.description: Match each graduate's specialization to what the facility needs.
Prioritise facilities with a serious staffing gap and disease burden.
Never staff a facility beyond its personnel capacity.

steps.title: The request
steps.user: Deploy 500 NYSC healthcare graduates to primary health centres across Nigeria. Match each graduate's specialization to what the facility needs, prioritise facilities with a serious disease burden, and never overload a facility.
steps.assistant:
Got it, here's what I understand:

- **graduates** → **facilities**
- **Objectives:** match specialization to facility need · prioritise critical disease burden · respect facility capacity

This is a replay of the recorded NYSC deployment run. Press **Play** or step through it.

steps.title: Data validated
steps.assistant:
Checked both tables:

- **500 graduates** (generated records)
- **750 facilities** sampled from 44,915 (GRID3 Nigeria, fixed random seed)
- Facility capacity, staffing, specialization and disease fields are augmented

Open the **Datasets** tab for a sample of both.

steps.title: Goals compiled
steps.assistant:
I've turned your goals into a scoring function the engine can evaluate for any possible plan:

- **Reward:** the graduate's specialization is accepted by the facility
- **Reward:** the facility has a high staffing gap and disease burden
- **Reward:** the facility receives at least one graduate
- **Penalty:** the facility is staffed beyond its capacity
- **Penalty:** the graduate is placed where their specialization is not accepted

**Shall I run it?**

steps.title: Engine routed, move model trained
steps.assistant:
Routed to the **evolutionary engine**. First it learns how good a single move is, so the search wastes less time on bad ones:

- **74,915** valid moves (59,932 train, 14,983 test)
- Fit on held-out moves: **R² 0.7818**, **RMSE 61.57**

These figures are from the version 3 run; the version 4 evaluation output was not retained.

steps.title: Five ordered batches
steps.assistant:
Placing **100 graduates at a time**. Each batch treats every earlier placement as fixed.

| Batch | Best fitness |
|---|---|
| 1 | 16,405 |
| 2 | 15,985 |
| 3 | 14,350 |
| 4 | 13,155 |
| 5 | not recorded |

Batches stopped early at generations 11 to 13.

steps.title: Verified clean-up passes
steps.assistant:
Two clean-up passes follow. A change is kept only if the real score allows it:

- Filled **94** empty facilities: 67,195 → **69,850**, kept
- Moved **66** graduates out of over-capacity facilities and fixed 2 mismatches: final **65,640**

The source does not break out the drop in the final pass.

steps.title: Result verified
steps.assistant:
Checked the finished plan against the data, version 3 beside version 4:

| Measure | Version 3 | Version 4 |
|---|---|---|
| Skill match | 409 of 500 (81.8%) | 409 of 500 (81.8%) |
| Facilities over capacity | 423 | 372 |
| Total excess staff | 1,915 | 1,826 |
| Final fitness | 63,920 | 65,640 |

Skill match is the same. Version 4's gain is structural: all **372** remaining over-capacity facilities come from staff already there, and no assigned graduate is placed in them.
